source_text:
Κατὰ
παράθεσιν, ὡς ἐπὶ σανίδων. Κατὰ συναλοιφὴν, ὡς ἐπὶ λαμπάδος ἐκ πυρὸς προερχομένης
καὶ αὖθις ἑνουμένης. Κατὰ οὐσίαν, ὡς ἐπὶ ἀτόμων, Πέτρου καὶ Παύλου, ἤ τινων ἵππων,
ἢ βοῶν, ἢ ἑτέρων ζώων.
Κατὰ σχέσιν, ὡς ἐπὶ φίλων καὶ γνωμῶν εἰς ἓν θέ λημα συνερχομένων.
thought_title: Modes of union: juxtaposition, coalescence, substance, relation
orientation: John of Damascus is listing the twelve modes of union with examples, and here he gives the examples for union according to juxtaposition, coalescence, substance, and relation.
pass_a_gloss: According to juxtaposition, as in the case of planks. According to coalescence, as in the case of a brand taken from fire and again being united to it. According to substance, as in the case of individuals, Peter and Paul, or of some horses, or oxen, or other animals. According to relation, as in the case of friends and intellects coming together into one will.

choices.why: The brief lists juxtaposition as one of the twelve modes; this rendering keeps the spatial sense of placing side by side.
The brief lists coalescence as a mode; the torch example shows merging into one while retaining continuity with the source.
The cast identifies Peter and Paul as examples of an individual (ἄτομον); this keeps the technical sense of indivisible concrete entities.
In the context of friends coming together into one will, γνώμη means a considered opinion or judgment, not a physical object.
The source has a space in θέ λημα, but the intended word is θέλημα, meaning will; the gloss renders it as will.

pass_b_english: Union according to juxtaposition occurs with planks. Union according to coalescence occurs with a torch that proceeds from fire and is then united again. Union according to substance occurs with individuals, such as Peter and Paul, or certain horses, or oxen, or other animals. Union according to relation occurs with friends and opinions coming together into one will.
notes: The source has a space in θέ λημα, likely a line break or minor scribal spacing; the intended word is θέλημα.

last_rejected.quote: friends and opinions coming together into one will
last_rejected.source_quote: φίλων καὶ γνωμῶν εἰς ἓν θέλημα συνερχομένων
last_rejected.why: γνωμῶν means 'minds' or 'purposes', not 'opinions'; misreads noun form.
last_rejected.fix: friends and minds coming together into one will
last_rejected.ruling: γνωμῶν can mean 'opinions'; rendering within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'person' for ὑπόστασις contexts; ἀτόμων here means individual persons.
last_rejected.fix: persons, such as Peter and Paul
last_rejected.ruling: ἀτόμων means 'individuals'; examples Peter/Paul clarify. No glossary term violated.

problems.quote: Union according to coalescence occurs with a torch that proceeds from fire and is then united again
problems.why: Torch 'proceeds from' fire then is 'united again' is physically unclear; what torch, what fire?
problems.fix: Clarify: a brand taken from fire and returned to it.

problems.quote: opinions coming together into one will
problems.why: 'Opinions' uniting into 'one will' is odd; likely 'minds' or 'intentions' (Greek gnōmai).
problems.fix: Translate as 'minds' or 'purposes coming into agreement.'

edits.old: Union according to coalescence occurs with a torch that proceeds from fire and is then united again.
edits.new: Union according to coalescence occurs with a brand taken from fire and then united to it again.

edits.old: Union according to relation occurs with friends and opinions coming together into one will.
edits.new: Union according to relation occurs with friends and minds coming together into one will.

fixed: Clarified the torch example as a brand taken from fire and returned to it.
Changed 'opinions' to 'minds' to reflect the Greek gnōmai more accurately.

problems.quote: friends and minds coming together into one will
problems.why: 'Minds' is odd for a union mode; likely translates Greek noi or dianoiai, but 'minds' as subjects of union is awkward and unclear.

edits.old: Union according to relation occurs with friends and minds coming together into one will.
edits.new: Union according to relation occurs with friends and intellects coming together into one will.

fixed: Changed 'minds' to 'intellects' in the relation example to better convey the Greek γνωμῶν as intelligent subjects of union.
